name: Umbundu
notes: Umbundu, Guthrie R.11, Bantu language of the Ovimbundu of central-southern Angola. Five vowel qualities a/e/i/o/u each with a nasal counterpart (nasality on vowels is contextual, driven by adjacent nasal consonants, not written separately). Prenasalized stops (mb, nd, ndj, ng) are single phonemes. Umbundu has an underlying two-level tone system (High/Low; Schadeberg 1990) whose surface realization includes downstep, so the practical orthography marks a first high with an acute accent (á), subsequent downstepped highs with further acute accents, and low tone with a grave accent (à); unmarked syllables continue the tone of the preceding syllable (Omniglot; Schadeberg 1990). Diacritics are not modelled as separate graphemes here; base-letter mappings are given.

sources.author: Schadeberg, Thilo C.
sources.title: A Sketch of Umbundu
sources.notes: Grammatical sketch of Umbundu; primary source for the augment/tone analysis (underlying High/Low tone with H-doubling, H-spreading, and final-lowering rules) and for the prenasalized-consonant and verb-stem facts.

sources.author: Ager, Simon
sources.title: Umbundu language, alphabet and pronunciation
sources.notes: Primary source for the three-tone (low/high/downstepped-high) orthographic accent system; corrects a prior two-tone claim.

ancestors.notes: Umbundu-Ndombe branch of Bantu (Guthrie R.10), within Atlantic-Congo.

location.notes: Approximate centre of the Ovimbundu highlands, central Angola.
